title: BLOOD ON EAR, HAND, AND FOOT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He then presented the other ram, the ram for the ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head. Moses slaughtered the ram and took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot." - Lev 8:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most memorable images in Leviticus. Blood applied to the ear, the thumb, and the toe.

The meaning is not hard to see. The ear — what he listens to. The hand — what he does. The foot — where he goes.

Hearing, working, walking. Almost everything a life consists of.

God claims all three. Not the ear only, as though faith were merely about receiving teaching. Not the hand only, as though it were merely about activity. Not the foot only, as though it were merely about attending the right places.

And the mark was blood — the same blood that made atonement. The consecration of Aaron's life was written in the language of sacrifice.

Paul brings all three together in his own way: Let the message of Christ dwell among you richly (the ear); whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus (the hand); walk in the way of love (Col 3:16-17; Eph 5:2).

Ask yourself three questions today. What am I listening to? What are my hands doing? Where are my feet taking me?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which of the three — ear, hand, or foot — is most out of step with my faith?
2. What am I regularly listening to that shapes me more than I realise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, claim my ears, my hands, and my feet. Let what I hear, what I do, and where I go all belong to You. Amen.
